title: Multi-Season Breakdown
text:
Compare player and team trends across the 2021–2022, 2022–2023, and 2023–2024 seasons.

2023-2024 Season

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Example multi-season dataset visual using diamonds/built-in high-volume data
diamonds %>%
  filter(carat > 0.5) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = carat, y = price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "magma") +
  theme_dark(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "2023–2024 Performance Metrics",
    subtitle = "High-Density Performance Trends",
    x = "Volume / Minutes",
    y = "Efficiency Rating"
  )

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text: For my final project, I plan to analyze NCAA Women’s Volleyball match and player statistics across Division I and Division II spanning recent seasons (2020–2025). The goal is to identify key performance metrics that differentiate top-tier teams and evaluate player impact across positions.

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text: For my final project, I plan to analyze NCAA Women’s Volleyball match and player statistics across Division I and Division II spanning recent seasons (2020–2025). The goal is to identify key performance metrics that differentiate top-tier teams and evaluate player impact across positions.

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Key Variables of Interest
The dataset contains thousands of observations detailing team performance and play-by-play actions sourced from Matt Waite’s repository and public data. The primary variables I plan to explore include:

Kills & Errors: Measuring offensive efficiency and unforced mistakes.
Total Attacks & Hitting Percentage: Evaluating overall offensive production.
Serve Receive & Digs: Analyzing defensive stability under pressure.
Blocks (Solo/Assists): Gauging net defense effectiveness.

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Exploratory Data Visualization
Below is an exploratory graphic examining the relationship between kills and errors across NCAA divisions:


Code
library(ggplot2)

# Sample exploratory data
set.seed(42)
n <- 120
vb_data <- data.frame(
  kills = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 25, sd = 5), rnorm(n/2, mean = 12, sd = 3)),
  errors = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 15, sd = 4), rnorm(n/2, mean = 6, sd = 2)),
  division = rep(c("Division I", "Division II"), each = n/2)
)

ggplot(vb_data, aes(x = errors, y = kills, color = division)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "NCAA Volleyball Performance",
    x = "Errors",
    y = "Kills",
    color = "Division"
  )








Figure 1: NCAA Volleyball: Kills vs. Errors by Division

title: Match Analysis: SMU vs. #2 Nebraska (Sept 3, 2024)
text:
Match Visualizations

Team Performance Comparison


Code
library(ggplot2)

team_data <- data.frame(
  Team = rep(c("SMU", "Nebraska"), each = 4),
  Metric = rep(c("Kills", "Digs", "Blocks", "Aces"), times = 2),
  Count = c(39, 43, 10, 7, 36, 36, 9, 1)
)

ggplot(team_data, aes(x = Metric, y = Count, fill = Team)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("SMU" = "#003366", "Nebraska" = "#D00000")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    title = "SMU vs. #2 Nebraska: Team Totals",
    subtitle = "September 3, 2024 Matchup",
    x = "",
    y = "Total",
    fill = "Team"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))








Figure 1: SMU vs Nebraska: Team Box Score Comparison







Top Hitters: Kills vs. Hitting Percentage


Code
hitters <- data.frame(
  Player = c("Naya Shime", "Maya Tabron", "Natalie Foster", "Merritt Beason", "Andi Jackson", "Harper Murray"),
  Team = c("SMU", "SMU", "SMU", "Nebraska", "Nebraska", "Nebraska"),
  Kills = c(9, 9, 8, 9, 8, 6),
  HittingPct = c(0.107, 0.292, 0.462, 0.107, 0.667, 0.045)
)

ggplot(hitters, aes(x = HittingPct, y = Kills, color = Team, label = Player)) +
  geom_point(size = 5) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("SMU" = "#003366", "Nebraska" = "#D00000")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 0.75)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(4, 11)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Top Hitters: Attack Volume vs. Efficiency",
    x = "Hitting Percentage",
    y = "Kills"
  )
